chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Writing for vocals, and the leader who demanded two charts a week
summary: Writing behind good singers was easier, while instrumentals took long; Dorsey let him write only when inspired, unlike another unnamed leader who demanded two arrangements weekly regardless.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you -- did it make any difference to you, as far as your feelings when you were writing arrangements, instrumental arrangements or backups for vocals, did it?

Well, I really liked to write for vocals, especially when they had singers like he had, you know, and it's easier to write fill ins, you know, when the singers are good, and it seems like the riffs come to you better, especially on the swing things, you know, plus the fact that
it consumed a little time, you know, saved time, rather, you know. You know, in instrumental, man, you got to really go all out the way.

It takes a lot of time, and you can't be repetitious but so much, and it took a long time. To be writing for a big band in those days, man, when you had to do two arrangements a week, it really consumed your time, you know. The only good part about it is you didn't have to be bothered with extracting part of the (unintelligible) in the scores. They did have copyists. all that was in copies. Of course, that was all in.

I tell you one thing I liked about Jimmy, though. For the time that I was with him, he never -- he would rush me. He'd say, "Now, well, do you feel like doing this? This week? Okay." He says, "do it, because the way you feel is going to show up in your work." He says, "If you don't feel like writing, don't write." You know, he was a great guy like that. Oh, man, he could play. He said -- Maybe one week you might feel like writing three, you know, or four. It all depends, he says. And he knew that I would write early in the morning, you know, and he agreed with me. It seems like the ideas come to you better when it's nice and quiet, you know.
But he was a great guy for that. I
was with another guy writing, and it was just the opposite. I had to make two a week for this particular man, you know, whether I felt like it or not. Sometimes --
-- just -- your arrangements sound just like that -- you didn't feel like it, and that was it. You've been through that bag, I'm sure.
Oh, yes. Who was that? Or do you want to mention names or --
We better get to the next band.

Okay, I won't press you on it. Were you -- at the most of the years that you were doing this arranging, I assume you were still playing at the same time, or did it -- did you go periods when you were arranging and then playing and then arranging?
